Kaweri Coffee Plantation Ltd.desc: A coffee-growing company in the Mubende area of Uganda, a subsidiary of the German firm Neumann Gruppe GmbH. It leases the land from the Ugandan state on a 99-year lease that began in 2001, and the company says it employs 250 people full-time, with up to 2,500 pickers at harvest (no year given for those figures).

sources.title: The project Kaweri

KazAvtoZhol.desc: A joint-stock company founded by the Government of Kazakhstan and designated the country's national highway management operator in 2013. It designs, builds, repairs and maintains the national road network and runs and collects tolls on toll roads; its shares were transferred to the Ministry for Investment and Development in September 2018.

sources.title: KazAutoZhol (Kazakhstan)

Khaou Chuly Development (KCD).desc: A Cambodian construction company, part of the Khaou Chuly Group, which was founded in 1955 and rebuilt after the Khmer Rouge period as Khaou Chuly MKK in partnership with Japan's MAEDA. The group builds buildings, public works, railways, dams and airports and also has interests in agribusiness, building materials, cement and other businesses; its chairman is Khaou Chuly and its president his son Khaou Phallaboth, and KCD holds 20% of the Socfin-KCD joint venture formed in 2007, with Luxembourg's Socfinasia holding 80%.

sources.title: Cambodia: Land cleared for rubber, rights bulldozed - the impact of rubber plantations by Socfin-KCD on indigenous communities in Bousra

Kharkiv Metro Company (Kharkivsky Metrop.desc: The municipal operator of the Kharkiv underground railway in Ukraine, a subsidiary of the Transport Department of Kharkiv City Council; the city council's executive committee sets its development plans and fares. Its Line III (Oleksiyivska) had eight stations at the time of the project appraisal.

sources.title: Kharkiv Metro Extension Project - Environmental and Social Documentation

Kilembe Mines Ltd.desc: A copper mining company in Uganda, 99% owned by the Ugandan government, which holds the Kilembe mining licence; it took the licence over after the concession of Tibet Hima Limited was cancelled in 2017. Its exploration licences expired in 2022 and the company was being wound up to make way for a new state mining company.

sources.title: Gov't seeks Shs2.6 billion waiver as Kilembe Mines winds up
sources.publisher: Parliament of Uganda (Knowledge and Oversight Bulletin)

Kinangop Wind Park Ltd.desc: The project company for a 60.8 MW wind farm in Kenya, about 60 km northwest of Nairobi, designed around 38 General Electric turbines at a cost of $150 million. It was majority-owned by the African Infrastructure Investment Fund 2, managed by African Infrastructure Investment Managers, with the Norwegian development fund Norfund holding the rest; AIIM lists the investment as exited.

sources.title: $150m Kenyan wind project reaches financial close
Exits: Kinangop

King Trader Ltd.desc: A Hong Kong company that owns the bulk carrier MV Solomon Trader, insured by the Korea Protection and Indemnity Club. The sources opened do not say what legal form it takes, where it is registered, how many ships it runs or its size.

sources.title: Hong Kong owner of cargo ship apologises to Solomon Islands over oil spill

Kinross Gold.desc: A gold mining company incorporated in Ontario with its principal office in Toronto, created by an amalgamation in May 1993; it files with Canadian securities regulators and the U.S. SEC. It produced 2,170,791 ounces of gold equivalent in 2024 and had about 6,800 employees at the end of that year.

sources.title: Kinross Gold 2024 Annual Information Form

Klong Dan Marine & Fishery and Palm Beac.desc: Palm Beach Development Co is a Thai company that bought small plots from villagers in 1989 and 1990 for a golf course and obtained title deeds covering public canals and flooded coastline; its major shareholders included Boonsri Pinkayans, wife of a former finance minister, Somporn, a brother of the politician Vatana Asavahame, and Northern Resource Co. Sources opened say only that Palm Beach later sold the land to Klong Dan Marine & Fishery, not what kind of company it is or who owns it.

sources.title: State could reclaim illegally sold Klong Dan project land

Korea Midland Power.desc: A South Korean electricity generating company, spun off from the state utility Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) in April 2001 and still a KEPCO subsidiary. It runs thermal, combined-cycle, pumped-storage hydro and renewable plants, with total capacity of more than 8,400 MW reported in 2016.

sources.title: One of the leading power generation companies in Korea

Korindo Group.desc: A privately held palm oil and timber business founded in 1969 in hardwood development, which moved into oil palm plantations in 1995. It grows oil palm and processes and trades crude palm oil and crude palm kernel oil through subsidiaries including PT Tunas Sawa Erma, PT Dongin Prabhawa, PT Papua Agro Lestari and PT Gelora Mandiri Membangun.

sources.title: Korindo Group company profile

Kun Hou Mining.desc: A gold dredging business owned by Chinese nationals, whose Congolese arm was registered in Kinshasa in January 2015 and is run by Michael Wang, who is also a director of Kun Hou Mining Group in Uganda; a French national, Franck Menard, is a minority shareholder. It ran four 25-metre mechanised river dredges on the Ulindi River in 2014 and 2015 and applied in 2015 to become a licensed gold trading house.

sources.title: River of Gold

Kyrgyzaltyn.desc: An open joint stock company set up under Kyrgyz law whose sole shareholder is the State Property Management Fund of the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic. Under an April 2022 settlement it took ownership of Kumtor Gold Company, Kumtor Operating Company and the Kumtor project from Centerra Gold, which bought back and cancelled Kyrgyzaltyn's shares in Centerra.

sources.title: Global Arrangement Agreement (Exhibit 99.1)
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Centerra Gold filing)

LNJ Bhilwara Group.desc: An Indian business group with interests in textiles, power generation and skills training, with members of the Jhunjhunwala family in its senior roles. Its listed textile arm, RSWM Limited, makes synthetic and blended yarns, fabrics and denim and reported turnover of Rs 2,771.03 crore in 2019-20; the sources opened give no figure for the group as a whole.

sources.title: RSWM Limited Annual Report 2019-20

Lafarge.desc: A building materials company making cement, aggregates, ready-mix concrete and asphalt, with its office in Paris and its shares listed on Euronext Paris. It reported net sales equivalent to about CHF 15,599 million for 2014, and merged with the Swiss group Holcim on 10 July 2015, with Holcim Ltd renamed LafargeHolcim Ltd.

sources.title: Registration Document relating to the public exchange offer for Lafarge shares
sources.publisher: Holcim Ltd / Autorite des marches financiers

sources.title: LafargeHolcim Annual Report 2015

Lafarge SA.desc: A building materials company making cement, aggregates, ready-mix concrete and asphalt, with its office in Paris and its shares listed on Euronext Paris. It reported net sales equivalent to about CHF 15,599 million for 2014, and merged with the Swiss group Holcim on 10 July 2015, with Holcim Ltd renamed LafargeHolcim Ltd.

sources.title: Registration Document relating to the public exchange offer for Lafarge shares
sources.publisher: Holcim Ltd / Autorite des marches financiers

sources.title: LafargeHolcim Annual Report 2015

Lafarge Surma Cement Ltd.desc: A Bangladeshi cement maker that built and runs an integrated dry-process cement plant on the Surma river at Chhatak, Sylhet district, fed with limestone quarried in Meghalaya, India, and carried in by overhead conveyor. Lafarge of France was to hold at least 51%, with the rest taken by the Islam group of Bangladesh, the IFC and other development institutions; the company was renamed LafargeHolcim Bangladesh Ltd in 2018.

sources.title: Lafarge Surma Cement, Summary of Project Information (Project 8035)
Lafarge Surma Cement changes name

Lafayette Mining Ltd (Lafayette Philippi.desc: An Australian mining company that owned the Rapu Rapu open-pit copper and zinc mine, holding 74% of the venture; it entered voluntary administration to try to avoid bankruptcy, after which the mine could be sold. The sources opened do not describe Lafayette Philippines Inc or Rapu-Rapu Minerals Inc.

sources.title: Administrators called in at Lafayette

Lake Turkana Wind Power Ltd.desc: The project company for a 310 MW wind farm of 365 turbines in the Rift Valley of northern Kenya. It was owned by its co-developers KP&P Africa B.V. and Aldwych International together with the turbine maker Vestas, the development finance institutions Norfund, Finnfund and IFU, and other private partners; its financing was signed in March 2014.

sources.title: Lake Turkana Wind Power project

Laos-China Railway Company.desc: A joint venture holding the build-operate-transfer concession for the China-Laos railway, signed with the Government of Laos in December 2016. Three Chinese state-owned enterprises hold 70% between them and one Lao state-owned enterprise holds 30%; it borrowed $3.54 billion from China Eximbank in June 2019.

sources.title: China Eximbank provides $3.54 billion of debt financing for China-Laos Railway Project

Larsen & Toubro.desc: An Indian engineering, procurement and construction company with its registered office in Mumbai, listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India. Its work spans infrastructure projects, energy projects and hi-tech manufacturing, and it reported turnover of Rs 1,42,509 crore and 56,465 employees for the year to 31 March 2025.

sources.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report 2024-25

Lavo Investments.desc: A company of Italian capital (written 'Lavos' or 'Lavos Investment' in the source), subcontracted in 2012 by Green Whells Dominicana to build the first stage of a waste-to-energy plant at the Rafey landfill in Santiago, Dominican Republic, and operating there from 2014. Recyclers and support groups believe Cilpen Global, which was given management of the recycling plant in 2016, is a subsidiary of it.

sources.title: Waste Picker Human Rights in the Dominican Republic: the Rafey landfill

Lihir Gold Limited.desc: A gold mining company whose flagship asset was the Lihir mine on Lihir Island, New Ireland Province, Papua New Guinea; it produced 230,000 ounces of gold in the first quarter of 2010. It agreed in May 2010 to be taken over by the Australian miner Newcrest Mining in a deal valuing it at A$9.5 billion.

sources.title: Lihir agrees to improved Newcrest offer
Lihir Gold accepts Newcrest bid

Linglong Tire.desc: Shandong Linglong Tyre Co., Ltd., a Chinese tyre maker listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It makes and sells passenger car, commercial vehicle and off-the-road tyres, both to vehicle makers and to the replacement market, and reported operating revenue of 22.058 billion yuan in 2024.

sources.title: Shandong Linglong Tyre Co., Ltd. 2024 Annual Report

Lukoil Overseas Karachaganak B.V. (Lukoi.desc: A Dutch company incorporated in Amsterdam in April 1999 that develops and produces oil and gas at the onshore Karachaganak field in Kazakhstan, holding a 13.5% interest in the production sharing agreement there. It is wholly owned by LUKOIL International Upstream Holding B.V. of Amsterdam, with PJSC LUKOIL of Moscow as ultimate parent, and reported net turnover of $532.6 million and total assets of $1.63 billion for 2023.

sources.title: LUKOIL Overseas Karachaganak B.V. annual accounts 2023
sources.publisher: Netherlands Chamber of Commerce filing (published by NOS)

sources.title: Parent Companies

Lukoil Overseas Shah Deniz.desc: A wholly owned subsidiary of Lukoil Overseas, the holding company that manages Lukoil's oil and gas exploration and production projects outside Russia. It holds a 10% interest in the offshore Shah Deniz gas and condensate field in Azerbaijan and borrowed $200 million from the EBRD, approved by the bank's board in January 2014.

sources.title: Lukoil Overseas: Shah Deniz Gas Condensate Field Develop. II (EBRD-45599)

Lundin Petroleum (later Lundin Energy, n.desc: A Stockholm-based energy company in the Lundin Group, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm as ORRON. It was a Norwegian-focused oil and gas company as Lundin Energy; that business was combined with Aker BP on 30 June 2022 and the company became a wind and hydro power company from 1 July 2022 under the name Orrön Energy, generating 335 GWh on a proportionate basis in 2022. The sources opened do not give the year the name Lundin Petroleum was dropped.

sources.title: Orron Energy Annual Report 2022
sources.publisher: Orron Energy AB / The Lundin Group

Lydian International.desc: A holding company incorporated in Jersey, originally registered in Alberta in February 2006 as Dawson Creek Capital Corp, whose shares traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange as LYD until they were delisted on 5 February 2020. Its main asset was the Amulsar gold project in Armenia, held through Lydian Armenia CJSC; it entered creditor protection in Ontario in December 2019 and a restructuring plan was implemented on 6 July 2020, with its winding up in Jersey pursued as part of that plan.

sources.title: First Affidavit of Victor Flores, Lydian International Limited et al (CCAA)

Lygend Resources & Technology.desc: A Chinese nickel company with its head office in the Yinzhou district of Ningbo, Zhejiang, listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (stock code 2245) since 1 December 2022. It sources and trades nickel ore, makes nickel products such as ferronickel and nickel-cobalt compounds for stainless steel and electric-vehicle batteries, and makes equipment; revenue was RMB 21.06 billion in 2023.

sources.title: Lygend Resources & Technology Co., Ltd. Annual Report 2023

MASEN (Moroccan Agency for Solar Energy).desc: A state-owned limited company in Morocco that develops and carries out the country's renewable energy projects, including solar, wind and hydro power, and is looking at green hydrogen. It is an accredited direct access entity of the Green Climate Fund, accredited in July 2021.

sources.title: Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (MASEN) - accredited entity profile

MASEN (Moroccan Agency for Sustainable E.desc: A state-owned limited company in Morocco that develops and carries out the country's renewable energy projects, including solar, wind and hydro power, and is looking at green hydrogen. It is an accredited direct access entity of the Green Climate Fund, accredited in July 2021.

sources.title: Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (MASEN) - accredited entity profile

MCC (China Metallurgical Group Corporati.desc: A Chinese state-owned enterprise. Under a reorganisation approved by the state assets regulator SASAC on 8 December 2015 it was merged into China Minmetals Corporation as a wholly owned subsidiary; it separately held 4.92% of the listed Metallurgical Corporation of China Ltd as at 31 December 2024.

sources.title: CMC and MCC meet in Beijing to discuss merger implementation
MCC 2024 Annual Results Announcement

Metallurgical Corporation of China (MCC).desc: Metallurgical Corporation of China Ltd., an engineering and construction company registered in Beijing, with A shares on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and H shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Its work covers metallurgical construction, housing and municipal infrastructure, mineral resources, equipment and real estate; operating revenue was RMB 552.0 billion in 2024, and its controlling shareholder as at December 2024 was China Minmetals Corporation with 44.26%, with SASAC as ultimate controller.

sources.title: MCC 2024 Annual Results Announcement

MECO S.A..desc: A Costa Rican construction company, founded in 1977 by Angel Cerdas and co-founded by his son Carlos Cerdas Araya, which began by renting out equipment. It builds roads, bridges and viaducts and works in Costa Rica, Nicaragua (from 1992), Guatemala, Honduras, Belize, El Salvador, Panama and Colombia.

sources.title: Carlos Cerdas, el multimillonario que empezo alquilando equipos

MIDROC Gold.desc: MIDROC, short for Mohammed International Development & Research Organization Companies, is owned by the Saudi billionaire Mohammed al-Amoudi and holds the licence for the Lega Dembi gold mine at Shakiso in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, first awarded in 1997 and renewed for a decade in April; the article says the company’s own website puts output there at 4.5 tonnes of gold (no year given). The source opened refers to Midroc and does not describe a separate entity called MIDROC Gold.

sources.title: Protesters demand Ethiopia cancel billionaire's gold licence

MIDROC group (Mohammed Hussein al-Amoudi.desc: MIDROC, short for Mohammed International Development & Research Organization Companies, is a group of companies owned by the Saudi billionaire Mohammed al-Amoudi. Among other businesses it mines gold in Ethiopia, where it holds the Lega Dembi licence near Shakiso.

sources.title: Protesters demand Ethiopia cancel billionaire's gold licence

MMG Limited (China Minmetals).desc: A mining company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under code 1208, whose major shareholder is the Chinese state group China Minmetals Corporation. It mines and processes copper, zinc and lead at Las Bambas in Peru, Kinsevere in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Khoemacau in Botswana and Dugald River and Rosebery in Australia, and produced 399,758 tonnes of copper in 2024.

sources.title: MMG Annual Report 2024

MP Energy (Melec PowerGen).desc: Melec PowerGen is an independent power producer, part of the Matelec Group, which holds a 20-year power purchase agreement with Senegal's state utility Senelec. Its 130 MW plant at Malicounda, about 85 km south of Dakar, uses seven Wartsila engines of 17 MW each and was expected to start operating in 2020. The sources opened do not describe an entity called MP Energy or say where the company is based.

sources.title: Malicounda, Senegal - IPP reference
Malicounda power project, Senegal

Macquarie Group.desc: A diversified financial group whose businesses are banking and financial services, asset management, investment banking and commodities and global markets, and which reports in Australian dollars. It made a net profit of A$3,522 million in the year to March 2024; the same page gives A$938.3 billion of assets under management as at 31 March 2023.

sources.title: Macquarie Group FY24 financial highlights

Madhya Pradesh State Forest Development.desc: Madhya Pradesh Rajya Van Vikas Nigam Ltd, a company incorporated under India's Companies Act on 24 July 1975, owned by the Government of Madhya Pradesh (Rs 37.93 crore of its Rs 39.32 crore paid-up capital) with the Government of India holding the remainder. It raises plantations of fast-growing and commercially useful tree species and manages state forests to increase their output.

sources.title: About the Nigam
sources.publisher: Madhya Pradesh Rajya Van Vikas Nigam / MP Forest Department

Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (.desc: A special purpose company that builds and runs metro rail projects in the Indian state of Maharashtra outside the Mumbai metropolitan region, including the Pune metro. It is owned 50:50 by the Government of India and the Government of Maharashtra, and the page describes it as a reconstitution of the earlier Nagpur Metro Rail Corporation Limited.

sources.title: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Limited (MAHA-METRO) - The Company

Malibya Agriculture.desc: An agricultural project set up by the Libyan Africa Investment Portfolio, run by its director Abdalilah Youssef, to grow rice and raise cattle in the Office du Niger area of Mali and to build the canals and roads for it. Under a convention dated May 2008 it was given 100,000 hectares of land in Mali for 50 years free of charge.

sources.title: Land Deal Brief: Malibya in Mali

Mando Machinery.desc: A South Korean car parts maker founded in October 1962, which traded as Mando Machinery Corporation from February 1980 until it became Mando Corporation in December 1999 and HL Mando in September 2022. It makes steering systems, brakes and suspension parts; as at 31 December 2025 HL Holdings held 30.25% of it.

sources.title: HL Mando Corporation (Formerly Mando Corporation)

Manitoba Hydro International.desc: A consulting and technology company wholly owned by the Canadian provincial utility Manitoba Hydro, incorporated in 1998. It advises utilities abroad on energy management, sells engineering and software products including the PSCAD power system simulator, and runs a rural Manitoba telecom business; it has more than 100 staff (no year given for that figure).

sources.title: Manitoba Hydro International backgrounder

Maple Energy plc / Maple Gas Corporation.desc: The IFC describes Maple as a privately held, Ireland-registered integrated energy company whose assets and operations are in Peru: oil and gas exploration and production, refining and marketing of fuels, gas-fired power generation and transmission, and a planned ethanol project. At the time of the IFC's 2007 disclosure it held a 100% working interest in Blocks 31B and 31D and leased the Pucallpa refinery from PetroPeru; the sources opened do not describe Maple Gas Corporation del Peru.

sources.title: Maple Energy - Environmental and Social Review Summary (Project 26110)

Marfrig.desc: Marfrig Global Foods S.A., a Brazilian meat company that processes cattle and makes beef and processed meat products in North and South America and consolidates the results of the food company BRF. Its shares trade on B3's Novo Mercado as MRFG3 with over-the-counter ADRs in the United States; net revenue was R$144.2 billion in 2024 and it had 126,832 employees at the end of that year.

sources.title: Marfrig Global Foods Management Report / Annual Report 2024

Maritsa East Mines.desc: Mini Maritsa Iztok EAD, a wholly state-owned Bulgarian lignite miner based at Radnevo and part of Bulgarian Energy Holding since September 2008, working a 240 sq km open-pit area under a 35-year concession agreed with the government in July 2008. It supplies lignite to the four thermal power plants of the Maritsa East complex, which generate more than 30% of Bulgaria's electricity.

sources.title: Mini Maritsa Iztok EAD

Mbada Mining (Mbada Diamonds).desc: A diamond mining company in Zimbabwe's Marange field, owned half by the Government of Zimbabwe through the Zimbabwe Mining Development Corporation and half by Grandwell Holdings, a company incorporated in Mauritius in 2009 and at first wholly owned by South Africa's New Reclamation Group; a Hong Kong company, Transfrontier Mining Limited, took 49.99% of Grandwell in 2010, giving it an indirect 25% of Mbada. It was licensed in 2009, its concession was expanded about sixfold to 7,540 hectares in 2011, it announced reaching US$1 billion in turnover in 2014, and the mining minister ordered it and other Marange companies to stop operating in February 2016.

sources.title: An Inside Job: Zimbabwe - the state, the security forces, and a decade of disappearing diamonds

Metropolitano.desc: Trenes Metropolitano, a private commuter rail operator in Buenos Aires, Argentina, led by chief executive Sergio Taselli, which held concessions to run the Belgrano and Roca lines from 1994 and the San Martin line until that contract was voided in 2004. It carried about 11.5 million passengers a month to 102 stations; the government rescinded its Roca and Belgrano concessions on 22 May 2007 and took the lines over.

sources.title: President Kirchner rescinds concessions of two major rail lines

Minera Andina del Sol (Barrick Gold).desc: A joint venture company formed in 2017 by Canada's Barrick Gold and China's Shandong Gold Mining, with each appointing three board members, after Shandong bought 50% of the Veladero mine in 2017. It manages the Veladero gold mine in San Juan province, Argentina, and oversees the Pascua-Lama project on the Chile-Argentina border, which has been shut since 2013.

sources.title: Barrick and Shandong join forces at Minera Andina del Sol
Barrick Gold sells a 50% interest in the Veladero mine to Shandong Gold

Minera Chinalco Perú (Chinalco).desc: The Peruvian subsidiary of Chinalco, the Aluminum Corporation of China, which runs the Toromocho mine in the Morococha district of Yauli province, Junin region, producing copper, silver and molybdenum. Chinalco acquired Toromocho in 2007 and production began in 2013.

sources.title: Chinalco begins work on $1.3bn Toromocho mine expansion in Peru

Minera Miski Mayo.desc: The operator of the open-pit Bayovar phosphate mine in the Sechura desert of Piura, Peru, described as a subsidiary of the Brazilian mining company Vale. The mine has capacity for 3.9 million tonnes of phosphate concentrate a year and started producing in July 2010; the Bayovar project itself is held 40% by Vale, 35% by Mosaic and 25% by Mitsui.

sources.title: Bayovar Phosphate Mine

Minera San Cristóbal S.A..desc: A Bolivian mining company that runs the San Cristobal open-pit mine in Nor Lipez province, Potosi department, producing zinc-silver and lead-silver concentrates, with offices in La Paz and Potosi. In February 2023 San Cristobal Mining Inc. of Canada bought the company from Japan's Sumitomo Corporation; in 2023 it produced 278,000 wet tonnes of zinc-silver concentrate and 77,000 of lead-silver concentrate, with 1,335 employees and 2,144 contractors.

sources.title: Minera San Cristobal Sustainability Report 2023

Minera San Rafael (Tahoe Resources).desc: The company that operates the Escobal silver mine at San Rafael Las Flores in Santa Rosa, Guatemala. It belonged to the Canadian miner Tahoe Resources until Pan American Silver bought Tahoe in a deal approved by both companies' shareholders in January 2019; the mine has been suspended since July 2017 under Guatemalan court rulings pending a consultation with indigenous people in the area.

sources.title: Guatemala: Pan American Silver, nueva propietaria de la minera San Rafael

Minera San Xavier (New Gold).desc: A wholly owned Mexican subsidiary of New Gold Inc. that operated the Cerro San Pedro gold and silver mine about 20 km northeast of the city of San Luis Potosi, producing about 95,500 ounces of gold and 1.5 million ounces of silver in 2009. New Gold was incorporated in 1980 as DRC Resources Corporation, took its present name in 2005 and has its head office in Vancouver.

sources.title: Cerro San Pedro Mine
New Gold Inc. Annual Information Form (Form 6-K)
Fenix (Salar del Hombre Muerto) Mine

Minera del Altiplano (FMC / Livent, now.note: Blanked. The only source cited, Mining Data Online’s Fenix (Salar del Hombre Muerto) page, redacts the operating company’s name (it shows “Mxxxxx xxx Axxxxxxxx S.A.”) and lists Rio Tinto at 100%, citing a Rio Tinto 2025 annual report. The page does confirm the mine facts — 350 km NW of Catamarca, lithium carbonate made at the on-site Fenix plant with some brine sent to the Guemes plant for lithium chloride, 17 kt of lithium carbonate in 2019 against 18,000 t/y nameplate — but it never names Minera del Altiplano, so nothing in it can be attached to the named company. FMC and Livent are not mentioned at all. A company register or a Rio Tinto / Arcadium filing naming Minera del Altiplano S.A. is needed.

Mineral Deposits Limited.desc: A mining company, quoted in Australian dollars, that held 50% of TiZir, an integrated mineral sands business producing titanium dioxide feedstock and zircon in Senegal and Norway. On 11 July 2018 France's Eramet announced it held 63.87% of the company's shares through an all-cash takeover offer of A$1.75 a share.

sources.title: ERAMET announces that it has acquired a controlling interest in Mineral Deposits Limited

Mineral Sands Resources.desc: Mineral Sands Resources Pty Ltd, a company 50% owned by the Australian-listed Mineral Commodities Ltd (AU:MRC) and linked to the Tormin mineral sands project. A court in South Africa placed it in provisional liquidation on the application of a secured creditor.

sources.title: Mineral Sands Resources faces provisional liquidation

Minerva.desc: Minerva S.A., trading as Minerva Foods, a meat company based in Barretos in the state of Sao Paulo, Brazil, which slaughters cattle and sells fresh beef, by-products, pork and poultry and exports live cattle. It runs 25 slaughterhouses in Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Argentina and Colombia with capacity for 26,380 head of cattle a day, and reported gross revenue of R$36.3 billion in 2024; the Vilela de Queiroz family began the business in 1957 and the IFC took a 3% stake in 2013.

sources.title: History and Corporate Profile
Minerva S.A. reports record 2024 financial results

Mitr Phol Sugar Corporation.desc: A Thai agribusiness that began as a family business in Ratchaburi province in 1946 and was formally established in 1956, chaired by Isara Vongkusolkit. It makes sugar, bio-power and bio-plastics and other products from sugarcane, and Thailand’s Board of Investment describes it as the largest sugar producer in Thailand and the second largest in the world.

sources.title: Mitr Phol Sugar
